description: Evolve minimal sorting networks - digital circuits that sort fixed-size inputs using compare-and-swap operations. Optimize for fewer comparators (gates) and lower depth (latency).

optimization_strategies.name: comparator_elimination
optimization_strategies.description: Remove redundant comparators that don't affect correctness
optimization_strategies.hint: Some comparators may be redundant given the sequence of prior comparisons

optimization_strategies.name: comparator_reordering
optimization_strategies.description: Reorder comparators to reduce depth while maintaining correctness
optimization_strategies.hint: Comparators on disjoint wires can be parallelized in the same stage

optimization_strategies.name: alternative_constructions
optimization_strategies.description: Try different sorting network constructions (odd-even, bitonic, Bose-Nelson, etc.)
optimization_strategies.hint: Different base algorithms may yield different comparator/depth tradeoffs

optimization_strategies.name: local_optimization
optimization_strategies.description: Make small local changes to comparator pairs
optimization_strategies.hint: Swapping or adjusting individual comparators may improve the network

optimization_strategies.name: hybrid_networks
optimization_strategies.description: Combine elements from different sorting network families
optimization_strategies.hint: Mixing constructions may find novel efficient networks

constraints: Network must correctly sort ALL possible inputs (verified via zero-one principle)
Comparators must be (i, j) tuples with 0 <= i < j < N
Solution must define N (input count) and NETWORK (list of comparators)
references: Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming Vol 3, Section 5.3.4
